top_story: Iran has entered a volatile succession moment as Ali Khamenei’s body lies in state in Tehran and the regime stages a week of funeral rites after the US-Israeli strike that killed him. This rupture follows months of open escalation, including Tehran’s March warning of a wider regional response after Donald Trump threatened Iran’s power grid and tied de-escalation to the Strait of Hormuz. The crisis is unfolding against the continued destruction of civilian life in Gaza, where Israeli strikes on beachside tent shelters hit displaced Palestinians already trapped by siege and famine. The emerging regional picture is one in which leadership shock in Iran, coercive US-Israeli pressure, and mass civilian harm in Gaza are reinforcing a broader war dynamic with little visible space for restraint.
